78: // parseStringComparisonEvaluationData tries to parse the input for the starts_with/ends_with evaluation.
79: // this evaluator requires an array containing exactly two strings.
80: // Note that, when used with jsonLogic, those two items can also have been objects in the original 'values' object,

82: // As an example, the following values object:
83: //

85: //	  "if": [
86: //			{
87: //				"starts_with": [{"var": "email"}, "user@faas"]
88: //			},
89: //			"red", null
90: //			]
91: //	}
92: //
93: // with the following data object:
94: //
95: // { "email": "user@faas.com" }
96: //
97: // will have been resolved to
98: //
99: // ["user@faas.com", "user@faas"]
100: //
101: // at the time this function is reached.
102: func parseStringComparisonEvaluationData(values interface{}) (string, string, error) {
103: 	parsed, ok := values.([]interface{})
104: 	if !ok {
105: 		return "", "", errors.New("[start/end]s_with evaluation is not an array")
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	if len(parsed) != 2 {
109: 		return "", "", errors.New("starts_with evaluation must contain a value and a comparison target")
110: 	}
111: 
112: 	property, ok := parsed[0].(string)
113: 	if !ok {
114: 		return "", "", errors.New("starts_with evaluation: property did not resolve to a string value")
115: 	}
116: 
117: 	targetValue, ok := parsed[1].(string)
118: 	if !ok {
119: 		return "", "", errors.New("starts_with evaluation: target value did not resolve to a string value")
120: 	}
121: 
122: 	return property, targetValue, nil
123: }
